name: Egyptians
also_known_as: the house of bondage (from Israel's view)
summary: The people of the Nile, whose civilisation was already ancient when Abraham visited. Egypt was Israel's refuge in famine, its house of bondage, the stage of the Exodus, a tempting ally for Judah's kings, and a hiding place for the infant Jesus. The prophets foresaw a day when God would call Egypt 'my people'.
name_meaning: Hebrew Mizraim (a dual form, perhaps 'the two lands' of Upper and Lower Egypt). 'Egypt' comes through Greek Aigyptos, probably from Hwt-ka-Ptah, a name of the temple of Ptah at Memphis.

origin.account: Mizraim was the second son of Ham. From him came the Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim, Pathrusim, Casluhim and Caphtorim — the peoples of Egypt and its neighbours. The Psalms call Egypt 'the land of Ham'. Historically, Egypt was unified under the first pharaohs about 3100 BC.

lineage.notes: Pathrusim = people of Pathros (Upper Egypt); Naphtuhim probably Lower Egypt; Lehabim probably Libyans. Egyptian women entered Israel's line: Hagar (mother of Ishmael) and Asenath, wife of Joseph and mother of Ephraim and Manasseh.

homeland.region: Egypt — the Nile valley and Delta
homeland.description: A narrow ribbon of fertile land along the Nile, widening into the Delta. The river's annual flood watered it, making it the breadbasket of the ancient world, and the deserts on either side protected it. Scripture distinguishes Lower Egypt (the Delta, where Goshen, Zoan and On lay) from Pathros (Upper Egypt, with No/Thebes).

places.name: Noph (Memphis)
places.note: Ancient capital, condemned by the prophets.

places.name: No / No-Amon (Thebes)
places.note: Great southern capital; its fall to Assyria (663 BC) is cited by Nahum.

places.name: Zoan (Tanis)
places.note: Delta capital; 'the field of Zoan' where God did wonders.

places.name: Raamses and Pithom
places.note: Treasure cities built by Israelite slaves.

places.name: Tahpanhes
places.note: Where Jeremiah was taken after Jerusalem's fall.

places.name: Alexandria
places.note: Hellenistic Jewish centre; home of Apollos.

timeline.event: Upper and Lower Egypt unified; the age of the pyramids follows (Old Kingdom, c. 2686–2181 BC).
Abram goes down to Egypt in a famine; Pharaoh takes Sarai and is plagued.
Joseph is sold into Egypt, rises to rule under Pharaoh, and saves Egypt and his family from famine. Israel settles in Goshen.
A new king 'which knew not Joseph' enslaves Israel. God sends ten plagues through Moses, and Israel crosses the Red Sea.
Solomon marries Pharaoh's daughter, who brings Gezer as her dowry; Egypt trades horses and chariots with him.
Shishak (Shoshenq I) plunders the Temple treasures in Rehoboam's fifth year.
Judah's reliance on Egypt against Assyria is condemned: 'the strength of Pharaoh shall be your shame'. Tirhakah of Ethiopia marches out.
Pharaoh Necho kills King Josiah at Megiddo and puts Jehoiakim on Judah's throne.
Judean refugees flee to Egypt, taking Jeremiah, against God's word.
Egypt ruled by Persia, then by Alexander and the Ptolemies; the Hebrew Scriptures are translated into Greek at Alexandria (the Septuagint).
Joseph, Mary and the child Jesus flee to Egypt from Herod: 'Out of Egypt have I called my son.'
Jews and proselytes from Egypt hear the apostles on the day of Pentecost.

religion.practices: Elaborate polytheism with animal-form gods, temples, a powerful priesthood, magicians and an intense focus on the afterlife. God said the Exodus plagues were judgement 'against all the gods of Egypt', and Pharaoh's magicians eventually admitted, 'This is the finger of God.'

importance: Egypt is the place from which God redeemed His people, and the Exodus became the defining act of salvation in the Old Testament: 'I am the LORD thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.' Passover commemorates it, and the New Testament presents Christ as 'our passover'. Egypt was also a place of preservation — for Abraham, for Jacob's family and for the child Jesus. Isaiah foresees Egypt joining Israel and Assyria in worship: 'Blessed be Egypt my people.'

impact.how: Rose from slavery and prison to second in the kingdom; saved many lives.
Raised as Pharaoh's daughter's son and 'learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians'.
Four centuries of sojourn, bondage and deliverance shaped the Law ('ye were strangers in the land of Egypt').
Killed at Megiddo opposing Pharaoh Necho.
Found safety in Egypt until Herod's death.

notable_people.name: Potiphar
notable_people.role: Captain of the guard who bought Joseph

notable_people.name: Asenath
notable_people.role: Joseph's wife, mother of Ephraim and Manasseh

notable_people.name: The Pharaoh of the Exodus
notable_people.role: Hardened his heart against God's command

notable_people.name: Shishak, So, Tirhakah, Necho, Hophra
notable_people.role: Pharaohs named in Kings, Chronicles and Jeremiah

key_verses.text: But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

For I will pass through the land of Egypt this night, and will smite all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgment: I am the LORD.
I am the LORD thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
Whom the LORD of hosts shall bless, saying, Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel mine inheritance.
And was there until the death of Herod: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Out of Egypt have I called my son.

fate.summary: Egypt was never destroyed, but it lost its independence. Ezekiel said 'it shall be the basest of the kingdoms'. Native pharaonic rule ended with the Persian conquest of 343 BC; Egypt was then ruled by Persians, Macedonian Greeks (the Ptolemies, until Cleopatra VII in 30 BC), Romans, Byzantines, Arabs, Ottomans and the British before independence in the 20th century.

today.summary: Modern Egyptians — over 100 million people — are the direct continuation of the Nile valley's ancient population, now largely Arabic-speaking and Muslim. Egypt's Coptic Christians (roughly 10% of the population by common estimates) trace their church to the apostle Mark, and their liturgical language, Coptic, is the last stage of the ancient Egyptian language.
today.descendants: The Egyptian people, Muslim and Coptic Christian.
today.modern_legacy: Pyramids, temples and hieroglyphs; the Septuagint (made in Alexandria); Egypt as one of Christianity's earliest heartlands.

archaeology.name: Merneptah Stele
archaeology.significance: Contains the earliest known mention of 'Israel' outside the Bible.

archaeology.name: Bubastite Portal, Karnak
archaeology.significance: Shoshenq I's list of conquered towns in Israel and Judah, matching Shishak's campaign.

archaeology.name: Beni Hasan tomb painting of Asiatics
archaeology.discovered: Tomb of Khnumhotep II, Beni Hasan
archaeology.significance: Shows a group of Semitic travellers in colourful garments entering Egypt, often compared to the patriarchal era.

archaeology.name: Elephantine papyri
archaeology.significance: Letters of a Jewish military colony in Egypt, including a request to rebuild its temple.
